text: When we look at the evolution of commerce, we've seen it transform from installed brick-and-mortar transactions to the advent of e-commerce, where this started off quite linear.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: A user would simply search and buy from e-commerce sites.

text: For us, we see AI as the next evolution in that journey.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: And with any evolution, we know two things to be true.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: The first, like all change, it can seem like a threat to a business.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: But on the flip side of that can also be seen as a big opportunity.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: And the second thing that we know is that whenever we have seen consumer behavior change because of a new technology, commerce tends to evolve alongside with it.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: And so we are starting to see that now with Argentic, where not only this is a new channel that's enabling merchants to engage with customers in a very deeply personalized way, but also how customers are searching and finding products is changing.

text: Earlier I touched on how the consumer behavior is starting to change, but I just want to dive deeper a little bit on this.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: When we think about consumer shopping,
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: That behavior up until today has been now what we're calling the search era.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: It goes through a phase where it's keywords, you're navigating a catalog, there's SEO strategies, and this is what most businesses have optimized towards over the last decade.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: And while for many businesses this worked, this model put the burden on the shopper to really find what they needed.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: Now what we're seeing is that we're moving into this phase called the intent error.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: So instead of typing keywords like, I want school supplies, I might say something like, you know, my daughter's starting school in September in fifth grade and I need to shop back to school.

text: And that's a very completely different interaction.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: So you are now expressing your needs in your own words and AI is now asked to meet you where you are.

text: And so the brands are coming to you instead of you having to go find them.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: And that's a very, very different interaction model.

text: And most businesses now are starting to find that they need to set themselves up for this interaction model.

text: What will have to happen is customers need to start trusting the recommendations that they're getting from the agents.

text: And once that trust starts to build, we do start to believe that they will start delegating more and more actions to their agents.

text: And that's also where, as PayPal, we're building towards is continue to build on that trust and move into a world where humans start to delegate more and more of their tasks in commerce and shopping to their agents.

text: And so these numbers don't just indicate that this is not meaningful now.

speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: So in a classic search, it might match literal words.

text: For example, I'm searching for blue running shoes.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: And you only get results that contain those words.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: The good part about this, it's very precise, it's fast, it's predictable.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: But the downside is it misses intent.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: And so if you ever search footwear for jogging, it may not even return those shoes.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: And that's only simply because of words that match.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: Whereas with semantic search, it matches based off meaning.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: What it does is it converts the query into vectors that create meanings of intent.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: And so you might type something, oh, I'm searching for something comfortable for marathon training, and you might find your running shoes, even though none of those words exist in the search query.

text: So the good part about that is it broadens on how you can search, but the downside is if you inject too much meaning, it can lose focus and hallucinate.
